_readme: Per-DJ effect settings for the Sound Engine (step 7, 2026-09-01).
When a beat is opened in the Sound Engine, the DJ's entry here decides
where every channel's knobs START. Nothing is printed at make time and
no beat file changes — this only pre-sets the rack so a beat arrives
sounding like its DJ instead of arriving flat. Every knob is still
yours to move, and Export writes a new file as it always has.
HOW A LANE IS MATCHED: a stem is named '<lane> - <sample name>.wav', so
'chord0 - piano stack ...' matches the 'chord' entry. Trailing digits
are stripped (bass0/bass1/bass2 -> bass, chord0/1/2 -> chord).
THE SUB IS NEVER TOUCHED. sub / bass / 808 lanes get no effects at all,
because the owner's mix rule treats the sub as the kick's low end and
leaves it alone. That list is _LOW_END in tools/crew.py:107 — this is a
deliberate copy, same as sound_engine/library.py copies the beats-root
lookup rather than importing the whole beat stack. Keep them in sync.
NOTE VALUES, NOT SECONDS: dly_note and br_note are fractions of a beat
turned into seconds against each beat's own tempo, so one setting works
at 88 bpm and at 150 bpm.
WHERE THESE NUMBERS CAME FROM: derived from each DJ's existing
character data in crew_config.json (drive, dust, vinyl, kick_dist,
mix_sat, space, era, and the 'listen' line), NOT invented. They are a
STARTING POINT tuned by ear afterwards — see DECISIONS.md.
Only four DJs are tuned so far: Otto Grit, Rage Engine, Glass Cat,
Night Metro. Everyone else falls through to _default, which is
deliberately gentle. Add entries as they get auditioned.

_default._other is the last resort for any lane nobody listed — reversefx, woods, vox, blips, claves, timbales, sirens and the rest. A whisper, so nothing sits bone dry beside a processed channel. The sub is still never reached: the low-end guard runs before any of this.

_default._notes: Barely-there glue. A DJ with no entry should sound like it does today, not like someone else.

Otto Grit._notes: 90s boom-bap, dust 0.5 + vinyl -42 + drive 1.35. Warm and dirty, top rolled off like an SP-1200. Hats are dead straight per the listen line, so NO stutter — that would fight his whole identity.

Rage Engine._notes: 150 bpm, kick_dist 6.0 and mix_sat 4.0 already in his config — the most aggressive DJ on the roster. Wall-to-wall 32nd hat rolls is his signature, so the stutter reinforces what he already does instead of inventing a trait.

Glass Cat._notes: Documented 'minimal and dry', zero dust, zero distortion, alt is literally dry. This entry is deliberately the quietest one here — if the system can't express restraint it is wrong. No stutter, no reverb push, one clean slap on the snap.

Night Metro._notes: Dark halftime at 140, kick_dist 5.0, drive 1.5, gated clap. Top end pulled down everywhere for the dark part; the stamp is a reversed cymbal so it gets the longest echo on the roster. Hat rolls ramp into the snare, so a light stutter fits.
